cards.explanation: The answer is the whole supply of food and water. Isaiah says the Lord GOD of Hosts is about to remove "…both supply and support: the whole supply of food and water…" (Isaiah 3:1). Food and water, friends. No pantry in the world is ready for that, and I own a LOT of ovens.

The answer is its leaders and advisers. After food and water, the list turns to people: the judge, the prophet, the elder, the counselor and more (Isaiah 3:2-3). These are the people folks look to when things get shaky. Take them away and everybody's looking around going, "Who's in charge?"

The answer is False. No kings from other nations are mentioned. God says, "I will make mere lads their leaders, and children will rule over them." (Isaiah 3:4). The replacements are lads and children, friends.

The answer is that they will oppress one another. Isaiah says, "The people will oppress one another, man against man, neighbor against neighbor…" (Isaiah 3:5). It's not an army from outside doing it. It's people turning on the folks right next to them. I think that's a hard thing to read.

The answer is rubble. The man says, "Take charge of this heap of rubble." (Isaiah 3:6). Think about that job posting for a second, friends. Come on in, we've got a heap of rubble, and the job is YOURS!

The answer is True. On that day the man cries aloud, "Do not make me leader of the people!" (Isaiah 3:7). He says he's no healer and has no food or clothing in his house. I think he knows exactly how big this mess is, and he wants no part of it.

The answer is that they spoke and acted against the LORD. Isaiah says, "…Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen because they spoke and acted against the LORD, defying His glorious presence." (Isaiah 3:8). Words and actions both, friends. The reason is given right there in the verse.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "…like Sodom they flaunt their sin; they do not conceal it." (Isaiah 3:9). Sodom was a city known for its sin (Genesis 19). There's no hiding going on here at all, because it's out in the open.

The answer is that it will be well with them, and it's good news in the middle of a heavy chapter. Isaiah says, "Tell the righteous it will be well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their labor." (Isaiah 3:10). A word of hope for the righteous. Don't skip over it, friends.

The answer is what their hands have done. Isaiah says, "…they will be repaid with what their hands have done." (Isaiah 3:11). The righteous enjoy the fruit of their labor, and the wicked get repaid for their own doing. Each one gets what their own hands made.

The answer is youths. God says, "Youths oppress My people, and women rule over them." (Isaiah 3:12). It matches the earlier line about lads as leaders (Isaiah 3:4). And notice He calls them "My people," friends. They belong to Him.

The answer is True, and it's God Himself saying it. "O My people, your guides mislead you; they turn you from your paths." (Isaiah 3:12). The ones meant to point the way are steering people off course. I think that's a heavy thing to hear, and He still calls them "My people."

The answer is the elders and leaders of His people. The verse says, "The LORD brings this charge against the elders and leaders of His people…" (Isaiah 3:14). Nothing here is hidden from view, friends. The charge goes straight to the ones in charge, and it doesn't wander off to anyone else.

The answer is poor. The LORD says, "You have devoured the vineyard; the plunder of the poor is in your houses." (Isaiah 3:14). It's a heavy charge. I think this one hurts to read, friends, and the next verse asks why they crush His people.
